title: Lay out a biosafety cabinet: 10 cm in, rear grille clear, clean to dirty
instruction: Set up this biosafety cabinet for work. The four items were left just inside the front grille, where they break the air curtain. Move each one onto the steel work tray at least 10 cm in from the front grille and off the rear grille, and lay them out clean to dirty from left to right: the clean supplies (the blue tip box and the media bottle) on the left, the culture plates in the middle and the grey discard pan on the right.
context: In a Class II biological safety cabinet the protective air curtain is drawn in through the front and rear grilles. Biosafety manuals (CDC/NIH BMBL Appendix A, cabinet makers' guides) tell users to place everything at least 10 cm (4 in) inside the front grille, never block the rear grille, and arrange the surface so work flows from clean to contaminated, typically left to right, so contaminated items are never passed over clean ones. Unlike VIMA-Bench sweep_without_exceeding (keep objects inside a marked zone) or RoboCasa DivideBasins (one item per basin) or the fume-hood solvent task (one bottle set back from the sash), every item must satisfy an inset and a keep-clear rule at once and the four must be ordered by their contamination class; no biosafety-cabinet task was found on the board or in AutoBio or LabUtopia. Done by: biological technicians, medical and clinical laboratory technologists (O*NET 19-4021.00, 29-2011.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Cabinet floor, all fixed 3 mm steel plates flush with each other, 72 cm wide (y -36 to +36): a dark front grille from x 16 to 20, a stainless work tray from x 20 to 46 and a dark rear grille from x 46 to 50. Low white walls (6 cm tall) along both sides at y +-36.5 and across the back at x 51. Four free items stand on the tray in a row at x 25, 5 cm inside the front grille, left to right: a grey discard pan (box 6.4 x 7 x 5 cm, 120 g) at y +10, a stack of culture plates (cylinder 6.8 cm across, 3.2 cm tall, 70 g) at y +3.3, a bottle of medium (cylinder 4.4 cm across, 8.5 cm tall, 180 g) at y -3.3 and a blue box of pipette tips (box 6 x 4.5 x 4 cm, 60 g) at y -10.
scoring: From a top photo and a ruler, with the grippers open. An item is placed when it stands upright (tilt under 10 degrees), still, on the tray with its whole footprint between x 30 (10 cm in from the front grille) and x 46 (the rear grille's edge) and inside the side walls. 0.15 for each placed item; 0.4 more when all four are placed and both clean items are left of the culture plates and the plates left of the discard pan, each by at least 3 cm between centres. Possible scores: 0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 1.0. Success: score 1, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the four items back in the row at x 25 in the start order (pan, plates, bottle, tips from left to right). The grilles, tray and walls do not move.
fidelity: Rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The cabinet is its floor and low walls only: no sash, window or airflow; the air curtain rule is judged from item footprints. Grilles are flat dark plates, not perforated. The plates are one solid cylinder, the tip box and discard pan solid boxes, and the bottle has no cap or neck.
